name: Stars of the Lid
label: Kranky
lede: Two guys who met in Austin on Christmas Day spent thirty years mailing each other tapes and making music so slow it barely admits to moving, and wrote a song named after Fulham's football ground along the way.

eras.title: Christmas Day in Austin
eras.text: Adam Wiltzie and Brian McBride started Stars of the Lid in Austin, where McBride had moved in 1990. Their early records were rough and tape-hissy, closer to drone rock than the orchestral stillness they became known for.

years.cap: Stars of the Lid · via Discogs
q: Your own personal cinema, located between your eye and eyelid.
years.src: Wikipedia · Wikipedia: Adam Wiltzie · Wikipedia: Brian McBride
years.h: Adam Wiltzie and Brian McBride form Stars of the Lid
years.p: Brian McBride, a debate kid from Irving, Texas, and Adam Wiltzie, a New Yorker whose youth tennis career ended with a knee injury at 16, start the band in Austin on Christmas Day 1992.
years.xp: McBride explained the name as the lights you see with your eyes shut: phosphenes, the shapes that float behind your eyelids. The pair loved Arvo Pärt, Gavin Bryars, Górecki, Brian Eno and [[Talk Talk|a74f43e4-50c4-4b19-a2ce-c05ce9bccb03]].

years.p: The debut, recorded in 1993 and 1994 with third member Kirk Laktas, comes out on the small Sedimental label. After it, Stars of the Lid is a duo for good.

years.h: Album two, and a split 12-inch with Labradford
years.p: Gravitational Pull vs. the Desire for an Aquatic Life comes out, and Stars of the Lid shares The Kahanek Incident, Vol. 3 split 12-inch with Richmond's [[Labradford|7cf7ef41-9637-4bf2-ae99-d8d6611ccdc6]] on Austin's Trance Syndicate.

eras.title: Twin Peaks and the DAT tapes
eras.text: Kranky signed them in 1997 and the records got longer, quieter and stranger. By 2001 Wiltzie was moving to Brussels and McBride was in Chicago, so they made a double album by mail.

years.h: The Ballasted Orchestra, first Stars of the Lid record on Kranky
years.p: Made in East Austin, it has two tracks titled "Music for Twin Peaks Episode #30" and a song named "Taphead" after the Talk Talk track. "The Artificial Pine Arch Song" runs 20:52 on vinyl.

years.h: 1998: an album, an EP and a split single
years.p: Per Aspera Ad Astra, the limited EP Maneuvering the Nocturnal Hum, and a split single with [[Windsor for the Derby|04fc2164-c46d-4d0d-851d-13467b444b84]].
The last single-disc studio album; the next two Stars of the Lid albums are both doubles.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Tired Sounds of Stars of the Lid
years.h: The Tired Sounds of Stars of the Lid, made by mailing DAT tapes
years.p: Adam Wiltzie was moving from Austin to Brussels and Brian McBride was in Chicago, so they sent DAT tapes back and forth. The 123-minute record sold about 5,000 at first and 10,000 within three years.
years.xp: Wiltzie worked on an Akai MPC 2000 and McBride on an Ensoniq ASR-10 sampler, each at home. "Gasfarming" samples dialogue from Twin Peaks. Pitchfork later ranked it the sixth best ambient album of all time.

eras.title: Brussels, Los Angeles and Kranky No. 100
eras.text: Both men made side records, then put everything into a second double album. It was Kranky's hundredth release, and it's the one most people mean when they say Stars of the Lid.

years.p: Adam Wiltzie teams with visual artist Christina Vantzou for [[The Dead Texan|18c2f08b-bdac-4877-9865-e5461317c1a6]], released on Kranky.

years.h: Brian McBride's solo album When the Detail Lost Its Freedom
years.p: Brian McBride's first record under his own name.

years.src: Wikipedia: And Their Refinement of the Decline
years.h: And Their Refinement of the Decline is Kranky's 100th release
years.p: Two hours long, made in Brussels and Los Angeles with cellists, brass, harp and the Saint-Jean-Baptiste au Béguinage children's choir. Metacritic scores it 87.
years.xp: "Don't Bother They're Here" uses the melody of Stephen Sondheim's "Send in the Clowns." "Dopamine Clouds Over Craven Cottage" is named for Fulham's ground, and by coincidence shares a name with Fulham's captain at the time.

years.h: A world tour with strings, and a tour-only CD
years.p: In Europe a string trio of Lucinda Chua, Noura Sanatian and Ela Baruch plays with the duo; Julia Kent plays cello in North America. The 59-minute Carte-de-Visite is sold on tour.

eras.title: One-offs and other bands
eras.text: Stars of the Lid never broke up, but after the tour it mostly lived in occasional shows. Wiltzie found a second audience with A Winged Victory for the Sullen, and McBride made music about disappearing bees.

years.h: Brian McBride scores Vanishing of the Bees
years.p: McBride's The Effective Disconnect is the soundtrack to the bee-colony documentary. He also starts Bell Gardens with Kenneth James Gibson.

years.h: Adam Wiltzie starts A Winged Victory for the Sullen
years.p: With composer Dustin O'Halloran, Wiltzie releases [[A Winged Victory for the Sullen|67c179d3-f358-43bf-8ecc-d9c560878b65]] on Erased Tapes.

eras.title: The unfinished album
eras.text: Brian McBride died in 2023 with an album's worth of Stars of the Lid sessions from the 2010s unreleased. Adam Wiltzie has said he wants to finish it.

years.cap: Stars of the Lid · via Discogs
years.p: Brian McBride, who lived in Los Angeles, died of natural causes at 53. Away from music he coached policy debate at USC and directed a University of Texas debate camp.

q: Someday I am going to try to do this for everyone.
years.h: Adam Wiltzie on the sessions Brian McBride left behind
years.p: Speaking to The Guardian from Brussels, Wiltzie says there's an album's worth of recordings from the 2010s and he intends to put it out someday.
